heading.en: A tree that never stops growing

hook.en: You will stop growing taller in a few years, but a coconut tree keeps adding new leaves at its tip all its life. Plant *growth* is open-ended.

say.en: You will stop growing taller in a few years, but a coconut tree keeps adding new leaves at its tip all its life. Plant growth is open-ended. In this lesson: Explain the open form of plant growth.
Describe the phases of growth and the sigmoid curve.
Compare arithmetic and geometric growth, and absolute and relative growth rates.

body.en: *Growth* is an irreversible, permanent increase in the size of an organ, its parts or even an individual cell, usually accompanied by metabolic processes that consume energy. Plants retain the capacity for unlimited growth throughout life because of meristems at certain locations; this is the open form of growth. Growth can be measured as increase in fresh weight, dry weight, length, area, volume or cell number. A single maize root apical meristem can give rise to more than 17,500 new cells per hour, while cells of a watermelon may increase in size by up to 3,50,000 times; growth of a pollen tube is measured in terms of its length. Growth has three phases: meristematic (cells with large nuclei and abundant plasmodesmata, near the root and shoot tips), elongation (increased vacuolation, cell enlargement and new wall deposition) and maturation (cells attain their maximal size in wall thickening and protoplasmic modification).

points.en: Open form of *growth*: new cells are always added by meristems.
Conditions: water, oxygen, nutrients and optimum temperature.

say.en: Behind the root tip we see three zones: the meristem that divides, the zone where cells elongate, and the zone where they mature.
In arithmetic growth only one daughter cell keeps dividing, so length rises in a straight line.
In geometric growth both daughter cells divide. Growth is slow at first, then exponential, then slows as resources run short: a sigmoid curve.
Two leaves each gain 5 square centimetres. The absolute growth is the same, but leaf A doubled while leaf B grew by only a tenth.

caption.en: In arithmetic growth only one daughter cell keeps dividing, so size rises in a straight line (Lt = L0 + rt), as in a root growing at a constant rate. In geometric growth both daughters keep dividing, so size grows exponentially (W1 = W0 e^rt). With limited nutrients growth slows and stops, giving an S-shaped (sigmoid) curve.
caption.kn: ಅಂಕಗಣಿತೀಯ ಬೆಳವಣಿಗೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಒಂದೇ ಮರಿಕೋಶ ವಿಭಜಿಸುತ್ತದೆ: ನೇರ ರೇಖೆ (Lt = L0 + rt). ಜ್ಯಾಮಿತೀಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಎರಡೂ ವಿಭಜಿಸುತ್ತವೆ: ಘಾತೀಯ (W1 = W0 e^rt). ಪೋಷಕಾಂಶ ಸೀಮಿತವಾದರೆ S ಆಕಾರದ ವಕ್ರ.

say.en: Pick a pattern of growth and watch the size over twenty days. Compare the absolute and relative growth rates.

body.en: In arithmetic *growth*, after mitosis only one daughter cell keeps dividing while the other differentiates and matures, e.g. a root elongating at a constant rate; length against time gives a straight line. In geometric growth both daughter cells keep dividing; growth is slow at first (lag phase), then rapid at an exponential rate (log or exponential phase), and finally slows as nutrients become limited (stationary phase), giving a sigmoid (S-shaped) curve typical of living organisms in a natural environment. Absolute growth rate is the growth per unit time; relative growth rate is the growth per unit time per unit initial parameter.

points.en: Relative *growth* rate = growth per unit time ÷ initial size.

problem.en: Leaf A grows from 5 cm² to 10 cm² and leaf B from 50 cm² to 55 cm² in the same time. Compare their absolute and relative growth.

steps.en: Absolute growth: A gains 10 − 5 = 5 cm²; B gains 55 − 50 = 5 cm². They are equal.
Relative growth of A = 5 ÷ 5 = 1 (100%); of B = 5 ÷ 50 = 0.1 (10%).
So A has a ten times higher relative growth rate.

answer.en: Equal absolute growth (5 cm²); relative growth A 100%, B 10%

narration.en: Let us work through this together. Leaf A grows from 5 cm² to 10 cm² and leaf B from 50 cm² to 55 cm² in the same time. Compare their absolute and relative growth.

say.en: Let us work through this together. Leaf A grows from 5 square centimetres to 10 square centimetres and leaf B from 50 square centimetres to 55 square centimetres in the same time. Compare their absolute and relative growth.
Absolute growth: A gains 10 minus 5 equals 5 square centimetres; B gains 55 minus 50 equals 5 square centimetres. They are equal.
Relative growth of A equals 5 divided by 5 equals 1 100 percent; of B equals 5 divided by 50 equals 0.1 10 percent.
So A has a ten times higher relative growth rate.
So the answer is Equal absolute growth 5 square centimetres; relative growth A 100 percent, B 10 percent.

problem.en: A root is 2 cm long and elongates arithmetically at r = 0.5 cm per day. How long is it after 8 days?

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A root is 2 cm long and elongates arithmetically at r = 0.5 cm per day. How long is it after 8 days?

say.en: Let us work through this together. A root is 2 centimetres long and elongates arithmetically at r equals 0.5 centimetres per day. How long is it after 8 days?
Use L t equals L 0 plus rt.
L 8 equals 2 plus 0.5 times 8 equals 2 plus 4.
L 8 equals 6 centimetres.
So the answer is 6 centimetres.

body.en: The sigmoid curve rises slowly (lag), shoots up (log or exponential), then flattens (stationary): like a new student who starts slowly, gets going, then levels off.
